place.name: Hotel drop-off & neighbourhood orientation
place.area: 汉庭北京隆福寺东四地铁站酒店
place.summary: Land at PKX early, DiDi to 汉庭北京隆福寺东四地铁站酒店 (东四北大街537号, by Dongsi metro). Stash luggage and do a short orientation walk — supermarket, pharmacy, DiDi pickup spots, Longfu Temple street, and Guijie (簋街) nearby.
highlights: Locate supermarket / pharmacy / DiDi pickup spots
Luggage storage if check-in is after 14:00
tips: Hotel check-in may be after 14:00 — use luggage storage if needed
Keep first meals within a short walk of the hotel
place.paceNote: Get settled, then head out — Guozijian and Yonghegong are minutes away.

place.name: Guozijian & Confucius Temple (国子监 · 孔庙)
place.summary: Imperial college and Confucius Temple — cypress trees, stele pavilions, and a calmer cultural stop than the palace. Very close to Beixinqiao / Yonghegong.
tips: Combo ticket usually covers both sites
Pair immediately with Yonghegong next door — same street corridor
place.photoNote: Cypress + red walls — lovely on overcast days.

place.name: Yonghegong Lama Temple (雍和宫)
place.summary: Active Tibetan Buddhist temple minutes from Beixinqiao — incense courtyards and a towering Buddha. Ideal first-day sightseeing without long DiDi rides.
highlights: Easy walk / short DiDi from the hotel
tips: Modest dress; buy tickets on site or via WeChat if queues look long
Morning is calmer, but afternoon still works after Guozijian
Combine with Guozijian — both sit on the same Yonghegong Street corridor
place.photoNote: Courtyard incense smoke + red walls — respect no-flash rules indoors.
place.paceNote: Keep it to the main halls if jet-lagged — no need to linger in every side court.

meal.name: 茶饼斋 · 北新桥店
meal.note: ~200m from Beixinqiao Exit A — easy first taste after hotel drop-off.

meal.name: 吴裕泰茶庄 · 北新桥总店
meal.note: Famous jasmine tea ice cream — light treat, photo-friendly packaging.

meal.name: 七寻八找胡同菜 · 雍和宫店
meal.note: Close to Guozijian / Yonghegong — share a few dishes for the table between temple stops.

meal.name: 郭通天宫院小吃 · 簋街店
meal.note: Close to Beixinqiao Exit B — classic snack sets without a long DiDi.

meal.name: 酸正正奶制品集合店 · 簋街店
meal.note: Optional dessert crawl on Ghost Street if the group still has energy.

place.name: Temple of Heaven Park (天坛公园)
place.summary: Ming–Qing complex where emperors prayed for good harvests. Circular Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests is Beijing’s most recognisable temple silhouette.
highlights: Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests
Locals practising tai chi / singing in the park (morning)
tips: Enter East Gate if using Tiantan Dongmen metro; DiDi can drop closer to the Hall
Combo ticket covers main halls
Morning light on the blue roof tiles is excellent for photos

ticket.detail: Combo ticket online or on site

place.photoNote: Walk a full circle around the Hall for symmetry shots; watch for drone bans.
place.paceNote: Skip distant park corners if jet-lagged from Day 1 — the Hall + axis is enough.

place.name: Qianmen / Dashilar stroll (前门 · 大栅栏)
place.summary: Rebuilt pedestrian street south of Tiananmen with snack shops and photo façades. Pair with your starred luzhu and dairy stops.
highlights: Snack hopping without another long DiDi
Easy exit back toward metro / DiDi
tips: Touristy — treat it as atmosphere + food, not deep history
Keep valuables zipped in crowds
place.paceNote: Speed through souvenir shops; spend time on food instead.

meal.name: 尹记门钉肉饼 · 天坛店
meal.note: Door-nail meat pies near Temple of Heaven — solid start before park entry.

meal.name: 恭敬李烤鸭 · 天坛路店
meal.note: Starred roast duck near the park — book or arrive slightly early for a table of 4.

meal.name: 味多美 · 天坛店
meal.note: Near Tiantan Donglu metro — coffee + pastry pause.

meal.name: 陈记卤煮小肠 · 廊房二条店
meal.note: Your starred luzhu shop near Qianmen — adventurous classic; order carefully for the less adventurous eaters.

meal.name: 三元梅园 · 前门店
meal.note: Court-style milk desserts — sweet finish on Qianmen Street.

pokemonCenter.name: Pokemon Pop-up · China World Mall
pokemonCenter.note: NEW official pop-up at 国贸商城南区 B1 WB120A/B — 10:00 opening, then DiDi south to Temple of Heaven.

place.name: Tiananmen Square (天安门广场)
place.summary: World’s largest city square — flag, Monument to the People’s Heroes, and the axis that leads into the Forbidden City. Security checks at every entrance.
highlights: Orientation photos before entering the palace
Sense of Beijing’s ceremonial north–south axis
tips: Enter via security with passport; no large bags / liquids rules can be strict
Skip dawn flag-raising unless the group is keen — it means a 05:00 wake-up
DiDi drop near Qianmen or walk from metro exits with less queue if possible
Chairman Mao Memorial Hall is on Thu 5 Nov with the National Museum instead
place.photoNote: Wide lenses help; morning haze is common — expose for the sky.
place.paceNote: Keep moving — the palace is the main event.

place.name: Palace Museum / Forbidden City (故宫博物院)
place.summary: Ming–Qing imperial palace — courtyards, throne halls, and endless red walls. South → north walking route ends at the Gate of Divine Prowess, steps from Jingshan.
highlights: Hall of Supreme Harmony & outer court grandeur
Treasure Gallery / Clock Gallery if time (extra ticket sometimes)
tips: Timed ticket required; passport name must match
Enter Meridian Gate (午门); exit Shenwu Gate (神武门) north
Rent audio guide or use a lightweight guidebook — reduces aimless walking for seniors
Rest on benches in side courts; don’t try to see every side gallery

ticket.detail: Real-name timed ticket via official site / WeChat

place.photoNote: Best red-wall / door details in soft late-morning light; watch for tour-group blocks.
place.paceNote: Worth speeding through the outer court if crowds thicken — protect time for Jingshan sunset views.

place.name: Jingshan Park (景山公园)
place.summary: Artificial hill north of the Forbidden City. Climb (or take it slow) to Wanchun Pavilion for the classic aerial photo of golden roofs.
highlights: City skyline beyond the palace walls
tips: Separate park ticket; enter south gate closest to Shenwu Gate exit
Stairs to the top — go at your own pace; one strong walker can scout while others rest mid-hill
Aim to arrive ~90 minutes before sunset for golden light
place.photoNote: Bring a short telephoto if you have one; phone wide + 2x also works.
place.paceNote: This is the photo payoff of the day — don’t skip it even if tired.

place.name: Pokemon Pop-up · CapitaMall Wangjing
place.summary: Official pop-up at CapitaMall Wangjing B1-27 — evening visit after Jingshan and hutong dinner. Skip if the palace day has already emptied the group.
highlights: Indoor sit-down after a long walking day
tips: DiDi from Nanluoguxiang / 汉庭 (~25–40 min); confirm mall hours before you go
Set a hard leave time — Great Wall is in three days and tomorrow is Xidan at 10:00
place.paceNote: Optional night add-on — Xidan tomorrow morning is the better stock stop.

meal.name: 贰柒松针包子
meal.note: Quick steam buns near Dongsi before heading to Tiananmen — or hotel breakfast if easier.

meal.name: Lunch near Forbidden City
meal.note: Eat before or after palace entry — options inside are limited and crowded. DiDi 10 mins to Dongsi if needed.

meal.name: 奇葩奶奶的烧鱼 · 酱肘子
meal.note: Hutong dinner after Jingshan — short DiDi north. Share fish + soy knuckle for the table.

place.name: Summer Palace (颐和园)
place.summary: Vast Qing imperial garden around Kunming Lake — Long Corridor, Tower of Buddhist Incense, marble boat, and willow-lined shores. One of Beijing’s best autumn photo sites.
highlights: Climb or view Tower of Buddhist Incense (pace yourself)
tips: Enter East Gate; through ticket recommended
Boat across the lake saves walking for seniors (seasonal)
Bring snacks — food options inside are pricey; you will arrive after the Xidan pop-up
DiDi drop at East Gate; same for pickup
place.photoNote: Bridge reflections and willow + lake frames work well into early afternoon light.
place.paceNote: Do not try to walk the entire lake circuit. Core loop: East Gate → Long Corridor → lakeside → exit. Skip distant Suzhou Street if tired.

meal.name: Summer Palace area lunch
meal.note: Eat just outside the East Gate after exiting — more choice than inside.

meal.name: Dinner near Zhongguancun or back at Guijie
meal.note: After Summer Palace, return to 刘阿妹鸡公煲 or 佬婆猪脚饭 near Beixinqiao if Haidian options feel thin.

pokemonCenter.name: Pokemon Pop-up · Xidan Joy City
pokemonCenter.note: B1 official pop-up + F1 Relax Party in the same mall — one DiDi drop covers both.

place.name: Chairman Mao Memorial Hall (毛主席纪念堂)
place.summary: Mausoleum on the south side of Tiananmen Square — next door to the National Museum. Solemn visit with queue and locker requirements. Do this first: mornings only (~08:00–12:00).
highlights: Queue culture tip: stay together as a group of 4
Lockers for bags / phones if required
tips: Arrive near opening — hall typically closes by noon; closed Mondays
Thu 5 Nov is open (Tue–Sun). Confirm 2026 hours the week before
If temporarily closed, continue to the National Museum without guilt
No photography inside

ticket.detail: Free entry; lockers may charge a small fee

place.paceNote: If the queue exceeds ~60 minutes, skip and protect time for the museum + Onix gym.

place.name: National Museum of China (中国国家博物馆)
place.summary: Massive state museum on the east side of Tiananmen Square — ancient China galleries, modern history, and rotating special exhibitions. Free with reservation. Same cluster as Mao Memorial Hall.
highlights: Warm indoor stretch before tomorrow’s Great Wall
tips: Reserve free tickets with passport names (Tue–Sun; closed Mondays — Thursday is fine)
Open ~09:00–17:00 (last entry ~16:00) — go after Mao Memorial
Pick 2–3 galleries max; the building is huge
Security queues — have passports ready

ticket.detail: Free reservation via official site / WeChat

place.paceNote: Speed is good here — quality over quantity so you still reach Xihongmen with energy.

place.name: Pokemon Official TCG Gym · Xihongmen (Onix)
place.summary: The other official Beijing Pokemon TCG gym (Onix) at Livat Xihongmen — DiDi south after the National Museum for the remaining official gym stamp (Day 4 is the Xidan pop-up).
highlights: TCG stock check after the Xidan pop-up (Day 4)
Indoor stop before an early night ahead of the Great Wall
tips: DiDi from Tiananmen / museum area to Xihongmen Livat (~45–70 min depending on traffic)
Confirm mall / gym unit on Amap (丽泽 / 西红门 Livat) before you drop
Set a shopping time limit — Great Wall is tomorrow
place.paceNote: Gym with purpose — not an all-day mall crawl before the Wall.

meal.name: Museum-area or Xihongmen mall lunch
meal.note: Eat near the museum before DiDi south, or at Livat after the Onix gym if the museum run goes long.

place.name: Mutianyu Great Wall (慕田峪长城)
place.summary: Scenic restored wall section northeast of Beijing. Cable car up (and optional toboggan down) makes this the best Great Wall choice for mixed ages versus crowded Badaling.
highlights: Cable car / toboggan logistics for the group
tips: Private DiDi / hired driver for 4 is strongly recommended
Leave 汉庭 / Dongsi by ~07:30–08:00
Cable car up for everyone; toboggan down only if weather is dry and seniors are comfortable
Bring water, snacks, tissues; toilets at base
Card / Alipay for tickets — keep passport ready

ticket.detail: Entry + cable car booked online where possible

place.photoNote: Best light mid-morning; haze can flatten distant ridges — embrace foreground towers.
place.paceNote: Walk a short wall segment between 2–3 towers, then return. No need to hike the entire ridge.

meal.name: Packed snacks + base-area lunch
meal.note: Eat at the village / base after descending — quality is average; fuel matters more than flavour today.

meal.name: 鼎香润 or 池记串吧
meal.note: Hearty dinner back in town — chaogan / zhizi BBQ style comfort food.

place.name: Beihai Park (北海公园)
place.summary: Imperial garden lake with White Dagoba views. Soft outdoor wind-down after Raffles City — skip if knees need a full rest.
highlights: Fangshan pastry tea house on the north shore (if open)
tips: Separate park ticket; short DiDi from Dongzhimen / 来福士 toward Beihai
Skip boat rides if temperature drops
place.paceNote: Truly optional — Raffles pop-up already makes a complete soft Pokemon morning.

place.name: Nanluoguxiang hutong loop (南锣鼓巷)
place.summary: Famous hutong spine — touristy main street, quieter side alleys. Good for snacks (紫光园 yogurt) near home if you still have energy after Raffles City.
highlights: Side-alley textures over the main souvenir strip
tips: Don’t walk the entire main street end-to-end — pick a short loop
Saturday is busier — stick to side alleys and keep the main strip short
place.paceNote: Speed through the commercial strip; linger in quieter alleys for photos.

meal.name: 穆羽斋清真包子铺
meal.note: Quick breakfast before the short hop to 来福士 for ~10:00 mall opening.

meal.note: Eat at 来福士 after the pop-up — easy sit-down before Beihai / hutongs.

meal.name: 紫光园酸奶站 · 南锣鼓巷店
meal.note: Classic thick Beijing yogurt — easy afternoon stop if you reach the hutongs.

meal.name: 南门涮肉 · 后海店
meal.note: Warming hotpot dinner — great for cool November evenings. Book ahead for 4.

place.name: Xidan Joy City — Pokemon Pop-up + Relax Party
place.summary: One mall, two Pokemon hits: official pop-up on B1 and Relax Party on F1. Best concentrated merch stop of the trip — do this at opening for stock before the campuses.
tips: Aim for mall opening (~10:00) — Sunday stock and queues are better early
Set a hard shopping cutoff so PKU / Tsinghua still get daylight
If pop-up queues are long, split the group (2 shop / 2 cafe)
place.photoNote: Indoor lighting — phone cameras fine; watch flash rules.

place.name: Peking University (北京大学)
place.summary: China’s flagship university — Weiming Lake, traditional gates, and autumn ginkgo walks. Visitor entry rules change often; check reservation / ID requirements before you go.
tips: Confirm current visitor policy / reservation the day before
Passport may be required at the gate
Keep it to a short photo loop — no need to cover the whole campus

ticket.detail: Visitor rules change often — reserve if required

place.photoNote: Lake reflections and ginkgo avenues — afternoon light still works.
place.paceNote: One lake circuit + gate photos is enough before DiDi to Tsinghua.

place.name: Tsinghua University (清华大学)
place.summary: Neighbouring campus to PKU — grand auditorium, ginkgo avenues, and classic academic architecture. Same Haidian cluster; short DiDi between the two.
tips: Check visitor entry rules (often reservation + ID)
Pair with PKU the same afternoon
Keep it shorter if Xidan ran long — one campus is still worthwhile

ticket.detail: Visitor rules change often — reserve if required

place.photoNote: Wide campus axes and tree tunnels — watch for bike traffic.
place.paceNote: Skip if legs are tired after PKU — one campus still makes the day worthwhile.

meal.name: Hotel breakfast at 汉庭
meal.note: Leave in time for Xidan Joy City opening (~10:00).

meal.name: Museum / Xidan mall lunch
meal.note: Joy City has plenty of sit-down options — easy for mixed diets before DiDi to Haidian.

meal.name: 四季民福 or 全聚德 (Peking duck)
meal.note: Farewell roast-duck dinner — pick 四季民福 (often easier for tourists / consistent quality) or classic 全聚德. Book a table for 4 ahead; choose a branch close to your evening route, not a far detour.

place.area: 海友北京首都机场南法信酒店
place.summary: Early checkout from 海友北京首都机场南法信酒店 (顺义南法信 / 顺平路), then a short DiDi to Beijing Capital International Airport Terminal 3 for SQ 805. Build buffer — Monday traffic and security queues.
tips: Target hotel departure ~06:15–06:30 for 08:45 flight (much closer than Dongsi)
SQ check-in counters — follow airport screens
Keep one warm layer until boarding; cabin can be cold

meal.note: Eat at the hotel if open, otherwise after security at T3.
